items.followUp: Define a molecule and distinguish between a homoatomic molecule and a heteroatomic molecule, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: A molecule is defined by its ability to exist independently and retain the substance’s chemical properties.
rubric.description: Defines a molecule as the smallest particle capable of independent existence and retaining the chemical properties of a substance.

rubric.why: Homoatomic molecules consist of atoms of the same element; the example identifies this type.
rubric.description: Identifies a homoatomic molecule as one made of atoms of the same element and gives a valid example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition and example.

rubric.why: Heteroatomic molecules consist of atoms of different elements; the example identifies this type.
rubric.description: Identifies a heteroatomic molecule as one made of atoms of different elements and gives a valid example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition and example.

rubric.why: The answer must distinguish the two types of molecules.
rubric.description: Clearly distinguishes molecules made from the same element from those made from different elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear comparison of the two types.

modelAnswer: A molecule is the smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and retain its chemical properties.
A homoatomic molecule contains atoms of the same element; examples include H2 and O2.
A heteroatomic molecule contains atoms of different elements; examples include H2O and CO2.

items.followUp: Define ionic compounds and describe four of their important properties.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds form through electron transfer and attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.description: Explains that ionic compounds consist of oppositely charged ions held together by electrostatic attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the nature or formation of an ionic compound.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds have an ordered solid structure.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds are crystalline solids.

rubric.why: Strong electrostatic attractions between ions require much energy to overcome.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds generally have high melting and boiling points.

rubric.why: Ions are mobile in molten or aqueous compounds but fixed in the solid lattice.
rubric.description: Describes electrical conductivity in molten or aqueous form, and/or lack of conductivity in the solid state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conductivity property.

rubric.why: Many ionic compounds dissolve in water or other polar solvents.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds are generally soluble in water or polar solvents.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds are made of positive and negative ions formed by transfer of electrons and held together by electrostatic attraction.
They are usually crystalline solids.
They generally have high melting and boiling points because the attractions between their ions are strong.
They conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but not in the solid state.
Many ionic compounds are soluble in water or other polar solvents.

items.followUp: Define vapour pressure and explain how temperature and the nature of a liquid affect it.

rubric.why: The definition describes the pressure of vapour in equilibrium with its liquid.
rubric.description: Defines vapour pressure as the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid in a closed container.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Heating increases the number of molecules able to escape from the liquid.
rubric.description: Explains that vapour pressure increases as temperature increases.

rubric.why: The strength of attraction between liquid particles affects how readily they escape into the vapour phase.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of the liquid’s nature or intermolecular forces on vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship.

rubric.why: A dissolved non-volatile substance reduces the tendency of solvent molecules to escape.
rubric.description: States that adding a non-volatile solute or impurity lowers the vapour pressure of a liquid.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid in a closed container.
Vapour pressure increases with an increase in temperature.
It depends on the nature of the liquid: stronger intermolecular forces give a lower vapour pressure, while weaker forces give a higher vapour pressure.
A dissolved non-volatile solute or impurity lowers the vapour pressure of the liquid.

items.followUp: Write four characteristics of a suspension.

rubric.why: A solution has a uniform composition throughout.
rubric.description: States that a solution is a homogeneous mixture.

rubric.why: The amounts of solute and solvent in a solution can vary.
rubric.description: States that the components of a solution can be present in variable proportions.

rubric.why: Solution particles remain dispersed and do not settle on standing.
rubric.description: States that solution particles do not settle on standing.

rubric.why: Dissolved particles are too small to be removed by ordinary filtration.
rubric.description: States that the components cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.

modelAnswer: A solution is a homogeneous mixture with uniform composition throughout.
Its components may be present in variable proportions.
Its particles do not settle on standing, so the solution is stable.
Its components cannot be separated by ordinary filtration because the dissolved particles pass through filter paper.

items.followUp: What is valency? Give the valency of oxygen as an example.

rubric.why: Valency describes an atom’s combining capacity, related to electrons lost, gained or shared.
rubric.description: Defines valency as the combining capacity of an atom or relates it to electrons lost, gained or shared.

rubric.why: A correct element and its valency provide the requested example.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of an element and its valency.

modelAnswer: Valency is the combining capacity of an atom, determined by the number of electrons it loses, gains or shares to form bonds.
For example, the valency of oxygen is 2.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a gram atom and a gram molecule, giving an example of each.

rubric.why: A gram atom is one atomic mass expressed in grams.
rubric.description: Defines a gram atom as the atomic mass of an element expressed in grams.

rubric.why: A gram molecule is one molecular mass expressed in grams.
rubric.description: Defines a gram molecule as the molecular mass of a substance expressed in grams.

modelAnswer: A gram atom is the atomic mass of an element expressed in grams; it contains one mole of atoms.
A gram molecule is the molecular mass of a substance expressed in grams; it contains one mole of molecules.

items.followUp: State two limitations of Rutherford’s atomic model.

rubric.why: Classical physics predicts that orbiting electrons would lose energy and collapse into the nucleus, contrary to atomic stability.
rubric.description: States that the model could not explain why revolving electrons do not radiate energy and fall into the nucleus.

rubric.why: The model did not account for the discrete line spectra of atoms.
rubric.description: States that the model could not explain the line spectra of atoms.

modelAnswer: Rutherford’s model could not explain the stability of the atom: revolving electrons should radiate energy, lose energy and spiral into the nucleus.
It could not explain the discrete line spectra of atoms.

items.followUp: State Mendeleev’s periodic law and explain how he arranged elements in his periodic table.

rubric.why: Mendeleev arranged elements mainly in order of increasing atomic mass.
rubric.description: States that elements were arranged in increasing order of atomic masses (atomic weights).

rubric.why: Elements with similar chemical properties were placed together in the same groups.
rubric.description: States that elements with similar properties were placed in the same groups or vertical columns.

modelAnswer: Mendeleev arranged the elements in order of increasing atomic masses (atomic weights).
He placed elements with similar chemical properties in the same vertical columns, called groups, so that their properties showed periodic repetition.
